name: Insulin (bodybuilding use)

card.summary: Prescription diabetes hormone injected by some bodybuilders for muscle fullness; evidence for benefit is thin and hypoglycemia has been linked to deaths.
card.note: Risk of severe hypoglycemia, coma and death; prohibited for non-diabetic athletes.

quick.overview:
Insulin is the body's main anabolic hormone and a prescription medicine for diabetes. Some bodybuilders have reportedly injected it, often alongside steroids and growth hormone, hoping for more protein synthesis, glycogen storage and fuller muscles.

A reference article states the evidence supports these effects only in a small group of drug-naive individuals, and that whether insulin improves performance is unclear.
quick.mechanism: Insulin promotes glucose uptake in muscle and fat, glycogen storage, amino-acid uptake and protein synthesis, and slows protein and fat breakdown.
quick.risks: The main risk is hypoglycemia, which can progress to seizures, coma, brain damage or death. Insulin misuse has been mentioned as a possible factor in bodybuilder deaths. It is prescription-only in many countries and banned for non-diabetic athletes.

lead: Insulin is a peptide hormone that regulates blood glucose and is the main anabolic hormone of the body: it helps muscle and fat take in glucose, increases amino-acid uptake and protein synthesis, and slows liver glucose production and breakdown of fat and protein.[1] As a medicine it is used for diabetes.[2]

Some bodybuilders have reportedly injected regular insulin, often alongside anabolic steroids and growth hormone, in the belief that it increases protein synthesis, muscle glycogen storage, strength and stamina.[2] The reference article states these effects are supported only in a small group of drug-naive individuals and notes that insulin misuse has been linked to some bodybuilder deaths.[2]
infobox: Prescription-only in the UK, EU and Canada
1921, Banting and Best, University of Toronto
Banned by the IOC for non-diabetic athletes since 1998

paras: Insulin was the first peptide hormone discovered, first isolated from dog pancreas in 1921 by Frederick Banting and Charles Best in John Macleod's laboratory in Toronto; Frederick Sanger sequenced it in 1951 and Dorothy Hodgkin determined its crystal structure in 1969.[1] It treats high blood glucose in diabetes and is prescription-only in Canada, the UK and the EU.[2]

According to the Wikipedia article on insulin as a medication, insulin was suggested as a performance aid around the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics, and the International Olympic Committee banned its use by non-diabetic athletes that year.[2] The article says some bodybuilders reportedly inject regular insulin before sugary meals, with steroids and growth hormone, and that benefits are supported only in a small group of drug-naive individuals.[2]

The article also cites allegations in the book Game of Shadows that baseball player Barry Bonds used insulin, and mentions insulin as a possible factor in the deaths of bodybuilders Ghent Wakefield and Rich Piana.[2]

The main risk is hypoglycemia, which can progress to confusion, seizures, coma, brain damage or death. Other effects include low blood potassium, allergic reactions in about 2 percent of people, and firm lumps from repeated injections at one site.[2] A 2008 report warned athletes combining insulin with growth hormone and IGF-I were exposing themselves to potential harm.[2]

No studies found of insulin as a bodybuilding or performance aid in healthy non-diabetic athletes in the sources reviewed. The reference article states that whether insulin improves athletic performance is unclear.[2]

timeline.event: Banting and Best isolate insulin in Toronto.[1]
The IOC bans insulin for non-diabetic athletes around the Nagano Winter Olympics.[2]
A report warns athletes combining insulin with GH and IGF-I risk harm.[2]

lore.intro: Insulin is discussed in bodybuilding communities under the nickname slin as a nutrient-partitioning tool.

claims.claim: Insulin drives nutrients into muscle for faster growth
claims.believers: Users say it increases glycogen storage, muscle fullness and protein synthesis.[2]
claims.experts: Effects are described as supported only in a small group of drug-naive individuals, and performance benefit is unclear.[2]

claims.claim: Insulin use can be managed safely
claims.believers: Some users say careful food intake avoids problems.
claims.experts: Hypoglycemia can cause coma, brain damage or death, and misuse has been mentioned in bodybuilder deaths.[2]
